hints: Brute force scans forward from every day: O(n²). Which days are still "waiting" when you reach day i?
If today is warmer than some waiting days, today answers all of them at once.
Keep a stack of waiting days (their temperatures don't increase going up). Pop while today is warmer.

insight.mnemonic: The hot day settles every colder debt.
insight.oneLiner: Keep unanswered days on a stack; a warmer day pops and answers every colder day on top.

recall.a: Indices of days without an answer yet; temperatures are non-increasing from bottom to top.
recall.q: What does the stack hold, and in what order?

recall.a: When it's popped by a strictly warmer day: answer = i − j.
recall.q: When is a day's answer written?

insight.why: Each index is pushed and popped once, so the 'nested' loop totals O(n). The stack stays non-increasing because anything colder than today gets answered and removed.

oneLiner: Keep unanswered days on a stack; a warmer day pops and answers every colder day on top.

pitfalls.explain: Only a strictly warmer day counts: pop while temperatures[top] < t, not <=.
pitfalls.title: Treated an equal temperature as warmer

pitfalls.explain: answer[j] is the number of days waited: i − j.
pitfalls.title: Stored the temperature or index instead of the wait

solutions.idea: For each day, look ahead until a warmer one appears.
solutions.name: Scan forward from each day

footnotes.text: Every day is pushed once and popped once - exactly when its warmer day arrives - so the nested loop is O(n) in total.

solutions.idea: Days wait on a stack until a warmer day pops them.
solutions.name: Monotonic stack

starter:
class Solution:
    def dailyTemperatures(self, temperatures: List[int]) -> List[int]:
statement: `temperatures[i]` is the temperature on day `i`. Return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the **number of days you'd wait after day `i` for a strictly warmer day**. If no warmer day ever comes, `answer[i]` is `0`.
title: Daily Temperatures
